title: Buddha (figure_10) crashes in NetworkContraction recarve: chord would cross a copy edge already held by an arc
description:
Loading ixdar-app/test/resources/quadlayout/figure_10/buddha_in_tri.off in QuadLayoutScene crashes during buildContractedTMesh. After `[contract] relabel floods=24148 faces=1554586 | 0.172s` the recarve throws:

```
java.lang.IllegalStateException: a chord in source face 139189 would cross copy edge 343364, already held by arc 5112
  at EmbeddedMeshTopology.acrossFreeEdge(EmbeddedMeshTopology.java:691)
  at EmbeddedMeshTopology.walkStrip(EmbeddedMeshTopology.java:613)
  at EmbeddedMeshTopology.layStraightSegment(EmbeddedMeshTopology.java:561)
  at EmbeddedMeshTopology.insertChord(EmbeddedMeshTopology.java:541)
  at SnappingCarve.appendChord(SnappingCarve.java:618)
  at SnappingCarve.layChords(SnappingCarve.java:588)
  at SnappingCarve.carve(SnappingCarve.java:359)
  at ArcNetworkRecarve.build(ArcNetworkRecarve.java:142)
  at NetworkContraction.recarve(NetworkContraction.java:227)
  at NetworkContraction.contract(NetworkContraction.java:158)
  at QuadLayoutEngine.buildContractedTMesh(QuadLayoutEngine.java:362)
```

The exception is uncaught (thread main dies), so the scene never reaches the failed-to-load handler. Two arcs of the contracted network want the same copy edge inside one source face: either the contracted network handed to ArcNetworkRecarve contains two arcs that geometrically overlap in that face (a contraction bug: an arc collapsed onto a neighbour without being merged or dropped), or the straight-segment walk in walkStrip picks the wrong strip through a face where a previously laid chord already claimed the edge, when a valid alternative routing exists. Buddha is the largest test mesh (1.55M faces after relabel), so this is the case that exercises many chords per source face.
definition-of-done: 1. Buddha (figure_10) loads in QuadLayoutScene through buildPatchSurfaces without an exception. 2. The root cause is identified and written on the ticket: either contraction emits overlapping arcs, or the chord walk claims an edge it could route around. 3. A pipeline failure inside rebuildLayout is reported through the scene's failed-to-load path instead of killing the main thread. 4. The other figure meshes that load today still load (hand, rockerarm, fandisk are covered by sibling tickets; check at least botijo and elk).
testing-plan: 1. Reproduce with a launch.json entry that opens QuadLayoutScene on buddha_in_tri.off. 2. Log at the failure site the two arcs involved (arc 5112 and the chord being laid), their node endpoints, and the source face; dump both to a small OFF or a screenshot region for inspection. 3. Decide whether the arcs coincide (contraction bug) or diverge (walk bug) and fix at that layer. 4. Reload buddha and capture a screenshot under tmp/. 5. Re-run the quad-layout tests that exist for the embedding package.
changes-made: Root cause (1 of 2), the walk-order bug: FaceStripPath.recordCrossing took the crossing position along a constraint edge as atLow/(atLow-atHigh) from ExactBarycentricOrient.area, which is plain floating point, while the edge itself was chosen by the exact orientation predicate in exitCorner. For a passage grazing an edge the two areas round to the same sign (buddha: atLow=-1.73e-18, atHigh=-8.67e-19 on arc 1740, source face 13330) and the position leaves [0,1] (2.0, and 4.0 for arc 9089 on edge 99886..99925). That position is the sort key grantCorners/mintLanes order the crossings on an edge by, so the arc landed on the lane at the wrong end of the edge; its chord then interleaved with another arc's inside one child triangle and walkStrip met an edge already held. So: not a contraction bug (the contracted network does not contain two overlapping arcs) and not a routing choice the walk could have avoided -- the crossing order handed to the carve was wrong before any chord was laid. Fix: FaceStripPath.crossingPosition takes the ratio of the area magnitudes, which equals the signed form wherever the signs agree and stays in [0,1] where they do not.

Root cause (2 of 2), found once the recarve passed: buddha then failed in LayoutResolution.measureArcLengths with '8 arc path steps measure zero'. FaceChordWalk.placeVertex decided on-edge by exact collinearity only, so a node handed the interpolated midpoint of an edge (which is never exactly on the line once the two ends carry chart coordinates) was placed by a face split beside the edge instead of splitting it. The edge survived, mintLanes later split it at the same parameter, and the two vertices held one chart position (buddha: node vertex 102192 and lane 114177, identical barycentrics in source face 114367). Fix: edgeParameterOf takes a point within FaceChordWalk.COINCIDENT_SEPARATION of the edge as on it, under a new nearCounts flag set only by placeVertex -- the carve walk keeps the exact test, since it refuses a claimed edge rather than skipping it.

Scene reporting: ModelScene.initModel caught only IOException, so a pipeline RuntimeException killed thread main before the scene came up. Both initModel and applyPendingModel now route through ModelScene.reportFailedLoad, which logs the path and the whole cause chain with its stack frames. Verified on botijo, which now reports ' failed to load ...: ArrangementDiagnosticException ...' and leaves the scene up instead of dying.

Diagnostics kept: EmbeddedMeshTopology.acrossFreeEdge now names the arc laying the chord (it only named the holder) and records blockedChordEdge/blockedChordHolderArc; SnappingCarve.appendChord catches the refusal and appends the blocked edge's endpoints plus every arc's passages through that source face, which is what made the two contending routes readable.

Verified: buddha (99370 V / 198736 F) loads through buildPatchSurfaces, '[recarve] nodes=4959 arcs=9914 patches=4957', screenshot at .claude/worktrees/patch-105/tmp/patch-105-buddha.png. elk still loads. botijo still fails, but identically on clean master (ArrangementDiagnosticException: arc 4824 could not be re-routed onto vertex 11156, same path and channel) -- pre-existing, same signature as PATCH-111 on block. Unit suite 226 tests green; HeapSamplerTest is flaky on this machine independently of the change.

Tests: unit.mesh.ConstraintStripTest gains aWellConditionedCrossingInterpolatesLinearly and aGrazingCrossingStaysOnItsEdge (hand-authored barycentrics that assert the exact predicate separates the endpoints while the doubles round together, so the fixture proves it exercises the pathological branch). New unit.mesh.NodePlacementOnEdgeTest covers the placement: both its tests fail with the nearCounts flag turned off, the second one exactly as buddha did (two copy vertices at one chart position).

Unknowns answered. (1) The contracted network does not contain two arcs sharing a segment: arcs 9091 and 5112 are distinct routes with distinct nodes, and the overlap only appears when the chords are laid, because the lanes were handed out in the wrong order along one constraint edge. (2) The failure is deterministic: three runs gave the identical arc 9091 / edge 343364 / source face 139189 / holder arc 5112. Alpha was not varied -- every run used the scene default of 15 degrees.
